question: In Figure 7B-2, what two alternatives are shown for signing the downstream end of the reduced school speed-limit zone?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Figure 7B-2 shows two alternative assemblies at the downstream end of the reduced school speed limit zone: an END SCHOOL SPEED LIMIT (S5-3) sign, or an END SCHOOL ZONE (S5-2) sign, each shown with an optional standard Speed Limit (R2-1) sign (SPEED LIMIT 45) mounted on the same post. The S5-3 sign is the required treatment as a general rule, while the S5-2 sign is a permitted alternative where the school zone ends at the same point. Standards (mandatory): - "Except as provided in Paragraph 4 of this Section, the downstream end of an authorized and posted reduced school speed limit zone shall be identified with an END SCHOOL SPEED LIMIT (S5-3) sign (see Figures 7B-1, 7B-2, and 7B-4)." Options (permitted): - "The downstream end of a designated school zone may be identified with an END SCHOOL ZONE (S5-2) sign (see Figures 7B-1 and 7B-2)." Visual evidence: [Image 1] Figure 7B-2 depicts, at both ends of the zone (for each direction of travel), an "END SCHOOL SPEED LIMIT" (S5-3) sign "OR" an "END SCHOOL ZONE" (S5-2) sign, each with an optional SPEED LIMIT 45 (R2-1) sign labeled "(optional)" mounted above it. [Image 3] The companion text page confirms the Standard for the S5-3 sign and the Option to use the S5-2 sign instead when the reduced school speed limit zone ends at the same point as the designated school zone, with a standard Speed Limit sign permitted on the same post above either sign. Citations: - Section 7B.05 Standard §3 (p.978) - Section 7B.02 Option §7 (p.976) - Figure 7B-2 (p.975) - Page 1021
gold_answer: An END SCHOOL SPEED LIMIT (S5-3) sign, or an END SCHOOL ZONE (S5-2) sign with a downstream Speed Limit (R2-1) sign shown as optional.
